text:
Gabriel Vilardi doesn't beat anyone with speed. NHL EDGE puts his top skating speed in the 4th percentile of the league. He beats them to the net instead, and lately it's working: a hat trick against Utah on Nov. 23, six goals and 13 points in his last ten games, and his ice time up more than two minutes over that stretch.

The funny part is that he's still behind. Seven goals on 10.7 expected goals (the quality of his chances) means even this hot run hasn't caught him up, and our numbers think his normal shooting is about 15%, against 12.3% now. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 99th percentile among forwards for chances from the home-plate area in front of the net last season. That's who he is: a big body who lives where goals are scored.

The caution is at five on five, where Winnipeg's share of the chances with him on is basically even. Evolving-Hockey valued him 34th among forwards last year, much of it from drawing penalties. Our range has him at 19 to 32 goals, and the hottest Jets team in weeks is leaning on him.
